query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism expected to operate across the test regime, predicts performance relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, specifies relevant temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a uniform dispersion of nano‐sized Y2O3 particles into the CoCrFeNi high‐entropy alloy will enable the formation of a stable, lubricious oxide film at high temperatures while also refining the microstructure to lower friction and wear at room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed polycrystalline CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix without dispersoids.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled volume fraction (e.g., ~3 wt%) of nano-scale Y2O3 particles uniformly dispersed within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
generation.conditions: Sliding wear tests conducted in ambient air under moderate sliding loads spanning a temperature range from room temperature up to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly distributed Y2O3 particles that pin grain boundaries and act as nucleation sites for an in situ formed lubricious oxide tribo-film.
generation.mechanism: At lower temperatures, the Y2O3 particles promote a refined microstructure and act as local solid lubricants, reducing the coefficient of friction and wear. At elevated temperatures, Y2O3 assists in the formation of a stable, adherent oxide tribo-film that mitigates adhesive wear and friction, overcoming the degradation typically seen in CoCrFeNi alloys under high-temperature sliding.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Y2O3-modified CoCrFeNi alloy should exhibit a consistently lower coefficient of friction and reduced wear rate across the full temperature range (room temperature to 800 °C) relative to the unmodified alloy.
generation.baseline: The standard, unmodified CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy which typically shows increasing friction and wear rates at high temperatures.
generation.boundary: Temperature range: room temperature to 800 °C; sliding loads typical for wear testing under ambient air conditions.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains in the optimized volume fraction of Y2O3, the long-term stability of the in situ tribo-film at extreme temperatures, and potential phase interactions within the matrix that may alter mechanical properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of baseline CoCrFeNi alloy and one set modified with ~3 wt% nano-scale Y2O3. Subject both sample sets to identical sliding wear tests in ambient air at controlled temperatures ranging from room temperature to 800 °C with a consistent applied load. Analyze wear tracks and measure friction coefficients at each temperature step.
measurements: Wear track depth and volume loss (via microscopy/profilometry)
Microstructural and phase analysis of worn surfaces (using SEM/XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Y2O3-modified samples do not show a statistically significant lower coefficient of friction and wear rate across the temperature range compared with the baseline samples, or if deleterious phase changes are observed that compromise surface integrity, then the hypothesis would be refuted.
